Use NA only where a criterion allows it. Then name decides_by: the id of the earliest phase after which decision_rule can be applied whichever outcome occurs, or "none". Root question: Can MEGADOCK’s GPU implementation make denser docking search affordable, and does that improve pose recovery within a fixed budget? Small pilot on exactly four unbound PINDER 2024-02 cases: 1aua__A1_P24280--1aua__A2_P24280:apo; 1ax2__A1_P16404--1ax2__A2_P16404:apo; 1dv1__A1_P24182--1dv1__B1_P24182:apo; 1nr5__A1_P07547--1nr5__A2_P07547:apo. Compare existing MEGADOCK CPU standard 3600 rotations, GPU standard 3600, and GPU documented dense 54000 (-D). Keep scoring and retained predictions fixed at 50. Pin prepared input bytes, references, binary/dependency/settings/thread/allocation identities. First establish execution correctness and scientific CPU/GPU agreement at identical settings using justified numerical tolerances sealed before fresh comparison. Then assess dense-search DockQ for rank1 and best50 separately, per case; native references only for evaluation. Calibrate runtime before choosing feasible common budgets; seal configurations, timing repetitions, comparison/noise rules and total spending cap before quality evaluation. Report complete workflow time, GPU activity and billed allocation cost, separating setup/retrieval from steady-state work. Keep acceleration, agreement and additional-search quality conclusions separate. Preserve negatives, unavailable budget arms and overruns. No biological efficacy or beyond-four-case inference. Run2 already exposed quality, so fresh executions are prospective replication under new rules, never unseen holdout or retrospective preregistration. Do not substitute throughput of bundled runs for this question. Run2 measured docking totals CPU/GPU/dense 40.07/6.85/69.38 seconds, not complete workflows; standard CPU/GPU transforms and DockQ matched, score max deltas 0.04/0.03/0.04/0.14 with no acceptance tolerance. Dense best50 improved all four observations, rank1 worsened in two including 1nr5. These are exploratory, not sealed conclusions. Historical H100 PCIe rate USD3.29/hour, setup145s, whole unscored bundle median131.9565s; old receipts setup/anchors/freeze/upload/profile/concurrency 145/1571/1402/1424/2832/3448s. Historical allocation and transport observations are estimates for a fresh box, not new producer measurements or public citations. Tree plans only, no box execution. Full card plan ceiling USD100; each later calibration must project below USD20 including setup, retrieval and idle, preferably USD5-10, soft6h/hard12h. Do not run full experiments on calibration route. Identify specific file/section gaps if existing routes cannot implement comparison. Tree PLAN can hold arms, anchor, decision_rule, noise_rule and phases. Measure compilation carries uncertain scalar inputs and phases, not arms/decision_rule; checks 2.5x PROXY or 3x other estimate bands, never scientific equivalence. Measure execution requires missing stage args/controller to be established. Card factual web sources may be checked; do not fabricate citations for private records.

card:question: Can running 2 or 4 independent CPU docking jobs together cut four-case workflow cost while preserving every retained pose?
card:hypothesis: Independent jobs may fill idle host capacity, making unchanged four-case CPU docking at least 1.05 times faster with identical outputs.
card:sequential_part: One workflow completes 4 fixed docking cases before producing its complete report.
card:method: none
card:if_lever: At width 2 or 4, both paired four-case workflow speedups reach 1.05 with exact docking and pose equality.
card:if_not: Neither width achieves 1.05 in both paired four-case workflow speedups, or output equality fails.
card:test_summary: Build separate CPU job commands and output checker; compare original four-case serial workflow, separate serial jobs, and 2/4 concurrent jobs in mirrored order. Require identical outputs and both measured speedups at least 1.05. Reserve 2 instance-hours, USD6.58, with USD10 hard cap.
card:closest_prior: Published MEGADOCK docking benchmarks reached 98% scaling at 420 nodes; they measured distributed work, not four jobs competing on one host [prior].
card:left_open: Whether 2 or 4 fixed-thread CPU jobs sharing 26 logical CPUs preserve every output and beat serial workflow time by 1.05.
card:anchor: Match frozen serial docking outputs and all 50 poses per case, then require identical outputs from each scheduling arm.
card:limits: No dense-search quality, GPU scheduling, biological efficacy or beyond-four-case inference; two repeats provide an operational screen, not statistical confidence.

Criteria:
stakes: Take the two outcomes this test predicts, as measured here and within the limits in scope_gap. 5 = whichever occurs, a choice someone faces (what to buy, build, collect or scale next) changes, and the test measures the quantity that choice depends on; 3 = the outcomes bear on that choice only through a step this test does not check (a stand-in system, simulation to reality, a single model), or one outcome is already much more likely than the other; 1 = neither outcome would change anything. Do not score how famous the field is or how close it is to the root question.
lever: Could the result tell if_lever from if_not, with compute the only thing that changed? Check four conditions: (a) the predicted difference between if_lever and if_not is larger than what noise_rule says run-to-run noise can produce; (b) compute_axis spans at least 10×; (c) the varied quantity is bought with compute, not with more data, labels or people (when restructuring.method is not none: the arms run on the same hardware and differ only in method); (d) inputs that could also explain the difference are in held_fixed. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail, or the measured quantity is not the one the question asks about.
verifiable: What is the measured outcome scored against? 5 = an exact or planted truth that does not come from the method under test (a simulation's hidden true run, an exact success flag, a formal checker, planted items), and the setup first reproduces a published number within a stated tolerance; 3 = labels from a model or human rater with an agreement check, or exact truth with no reproduction step; 1 = nothing independent of the method's own output.
open: Does the closest published result already answer this question over this range? 5 = the quoted prior stops short of this range or asks a different question, and the plan states the gap; 3 = the prior answers part of it (a narrower range, a related system), or no prior is named; 1 = the quoted prior already answers it. Reusing published tools, models or benchmarks does not lower this score.
reshape: Does the plan remove a step-after-step dependency that one answer waits on, rather than run independent work side by side? 5 = restructuring names the dependency, why it need not run in order and how the plan computes it at the same time; condition says what must hold for that to pay off; condition_phase measures it before the main spend; and the closest prior does not already do this for this system; 3 = it removes a dependency, but condition is missing or is not measured before the main spend; 2 = it parallelises only within each step (splitting a large state across GPUs) or regroups and rebalances independent work (batching unfinished runs, load balancing, lower precision), leaving the chain in order; 1 = independent copies side by side, or one job per GPU, is the only parallelism, or the plan rebuilds a parallel version the closest prior already reports for this system. Reusing a method published for a different system does not lower this score.
baseline: Is the gain timed against the strongest ways to get the same answer without the plan's method? Check four conditions: (a) baseline_sequential is tuned (compiled, vectorised or multithreaded code, or a published optimised code), not a plain interpreted loop; (b) baseline_copies is timed on the same GPUs; (c) anchor checks the parallel result against the sequential one within a stated tolerance; (d) a named phase times every arm as time or dollars to one answer, so the gain is measured, not only modelled. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail. NA when restructuring.method is none.

Card:
card:question: Can running 2 or 4 independent CPU docking jobs together cut four-case workflow cost while preserving every retained pose?
card:hypothesis: Independent jobs may fill idle host capacity, making unchanged four-case CPU docking at least 1.05 times faster with identical outputs.
card:sequential_part: One workflow completes 4 fixed docking cases before producing its complete report.
card:method: none
card:if_lever: At width 2 or 4, both paired four-case workflow speedups reach 1.05 with exact docking and pose equality.
card:if_not: Neither width achieves 1.05 in both paired four-case workflow speedups, or output equality fails.
card:test_summary: Build separate CPU job commands and output checker; compare original four-case serial workflow, separate serial jobs, and 2/4 concurrent jobs in mirrored order. Require identical outputs and both measured speedups at least 1.05. Reserve 2 instance-hours, USD6.58, with USD10 hard cap.
card:closest_prior: Published MEGADOCK docking benchmarks reached 98% scaling at 420 nodes; they measured distributed work, not four jobs competing on one host [prior].
card:left_open: Whether 2 or 4 fixed-thread CPU jobs sharing 26 logical CPUs preserve every output and beat serial workflow time by 1.05.
card:anchor: Match frozen serial docking outputs and all 50 poses per case, then require identical outputs from each scheduling arm.
card:limits: No dense-search quality, GPU scheduling, biological efficacy or beyond-four-case inference; two repeats provide an operational screen, not statistical confidence.

Criteria:
stakes: Take the two outcomes this test predicts, as measured here and within the limits in scope_gap. 5 = whichever occurs, a choice someone faces (what to buy, build, collect or scale next) changes, and the test measures the quantity that choice depends on; 3 = the outcomes bear on that choice only through a step this test does not check (a stand-in system, simulation to reality, a single model), or one outcome is already much more likely than the other; 1 = neither outcome would change anything. Do not score how famous the field is or how close it is to the root question.
lever: Could the result tell if_lever from if_not, with compute the only thing that changed? Check four conditions: (a) the predicted difference between if_lever and if_not is larger than what noise_rule says run-to-run noise can produce; (b) compute_axis spans at least 10×; (c) the varied quantity is bought with compute, not with more data, labels or people (when restructuring.method is not none: the arms run on the same hardware and differ only in method); (d) inputs that could also explain the difference are in held_fixed. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail, or the measured quantity is not the one the question asks about.
verifiable: What is the measured outcome scored against? 5 = an exact or planted truth that does not come from the method under test (a simulation's hidden true run, an exact success flag, a formal checker, planted items), and the setup first reproduces a published number within a stated tolerance; 3 = labels from a model or human rater with an agreement check, or exact truth with no reproduction step; 1 = nothing independent of the method's own output.
open: Does the closest published result already answer this question over this range? 5 = the quoted prior stops short of this range or asks a different question, and the plan states the gap; 3 = the prior answers part of it (a narrower range, a related system), or no prior is named; 1 = the quoted prior already answers it. Reusing published tools, models or benchmarks does not lower this score.
reshape: Does the plan remove a step-after-step dependency that one answer waits on, rather than run independent work side by side? 5 = restructuring names the dependency, why it need not run in order and how the plan computes it at the same time; condition says what must hold for that to pay off; condition_phase measures it before the main spend; and the closest prior does not already do this for this system; 3 = it removes a dependency, but condition is missing or is not measured before the main spend; 2 = it parallelises only within each step (splitting a large state across GPUs) or regroups and rebalances independent work (batching unfinished runs, load balancing, lower precision), leaving the chain in order; 1 = independent copies side by side, or one job per GPU, is the only parallelism, or the plan rebuilds a parallel version the closest prior already reports for this system. Reusing a method published for a different system does not lower this score.
baseline: Is the gain timed against the strongest ways to get the same answer without the plan's method? Check four conditions: (a) baseline_sequential is tuned (compiled, vectorised or multithreaded code, or a published optimised code), not a plain interpreted loop; (b) baseline_copies is timed on the same GPUs; (c) anchor checks the parallel result against the sequential one within a stated tolerance; (d) a named phase times every arm as time or dollars to one answer, so the gain is measured, not only modelled. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail. NA when restructuring.method is none.
